correctness.rationale: Unit normals correspond bijectively to fixed-norm zero-sum simplex projection vectors; each nonempty signed partition yields a strictly convex lower-bounded equal-total energy problem. The minimum common total is the larger bound sum and the unique optimizer is the exact water-filled profile. The smallest partition energy yields the sharp blocking scale, and equality forces the specified profile. Open-ball boundary, pairwise separation and interior-point radius follow by direct center distances and triangle inequality. Checked source package check.py passed 119 exact-weight profiles and 4,760 sampled directions, but universal proof is analytic.

Read the two nearest published mathematical-record results in full and compared mathematical implications. Historical non-indexed sources and general convex-programming formulations remain a material priority risk.
residual_risks: No comprehensive historical-priority claim is made; earlier weighted Chebyshev/projective avoidance formulations may exist under different terminology.
Gritzmann–Klee (1992) and Alexander (1977) were corroborated via explicit later derivations but their entire historical full texts were not examined.
The finite checker cannot certify every continuous input; its role is only to corroborate the analytic argument.

value.rationale: A complete exact inverse threshold for every positive unequal radius profile of a natural vertex-centered ball family; unique water-filling active profiles and all minimizing sign partitions replace continuous geometry with a finite classification. It supplies nontrivial, unequal-disconnected ball examples with an interior hyperplane-nonconvexity region, and the three-magnitude (1,1,1,2) example is not a renamed classical equal-width bound. It is structural and naturally linked to the nonconvexity-point construction, not an unmotivated one-off parameter.
